issues.description: Template repository's Farm implementation is structurally broken and misnamed: the file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java defines a class AnimalFarm (not Farm), contains duplicated/embedded package and class declarations and invalid nested content which will not compile. This conflicts with the problem statement UML and with Main.java which expects a class named Farm. As a result students cannot compile or run the starter code, cannot add animals to the expected Farm class, and will be blocked from implementing the intended design.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the broken template file contents with a proper Farm class declaration matching the UML and the solution: declare public class Farm in package de.tum.cit.ase, remove duplicated 'package' and nested class fragments, provide the animals List<Animal> field, a no-arg constructor that initializes the ArrayList, and the public methods addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), singFarmSong(), and appropriate getter/setter. Ensure the class name is Farm so Main.java and student code compile and align with the problem specification.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to the core class as 'Farm', but the template declares a class named 'AnimalFarm' inside src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java. This mismatch (file named Farm.java containing public class AnimalFarm) breaks the expected mapping between the exercise description and the starter code, likely confusing students who look for a 'Farm' class to implement/extend and causing compile/usage issues when other template code (e.g., Main) expects 'Farm'.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template to 'Farm' (matching the problem statement and solution) and ensure the public class name matches the file name. Update any internal references in the template to use 'Farm' so students can clearly map requirements to the provided starter code.
